analysis.reading:
THREE WORDS, THREE UNRELATED FIELDS, NO COMPOUND. "Doxastic" pulls Collins Dictionary and a PhilPapers bibliography on belief revision — AGM theory, Hintikka 1962. "Calcification" pulls SOFT TISSUE CALCIFICATION from ScienceDirect: "tissue becomes hardened by deposition of calcium salts, which normally occurs only in bone and teeth." "Regulatory" pulls an Oklahoma free-market think-tank on rule accumulation impeding growth, and a LinkedIn argument about an FDA for AI.

This is the decomposition pattern seen at «"metadata as theology"» and «acanthian dove», but at three components rather than two, and with no archive card at all. The layer read the phrase as "a playful amalgamation of distinct concepts" — its own words — and then supplied the concepts.

The medical sense is the sharpest accident: the archive means belief systems hardening into unexaminable rule; ScienceDirect means calcium depositing where it should not. The metaphor the coinage relies on is retrieved as its literal source.
